content.text:
The failed response is **not retained**. The client reads response bytes and immediately deserializes them. On failure, it converts only the Serde error text into `ResponseError`; the body, HTTP status, request URL, member ID, and page offset are absent from that error. It also never checks HTTP status, so an upstream HTTP error body can appear as `missing field totalResults`. That cause remains a hypothesis. See [declarations.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/outbound/parliament_api/declarations.rs:27) and [parliament_api.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/outbound/parliament_api.rs:160).

Successful declaration items retain their source JSON, which is written to Parquet only after every page for that member succeeds. A failed member therefore has no newly written partition, including any earlier successful pages from that request sequence. Other completed members can have files already written. See [declaration_source.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/outbound/declaration_source.rs:180), [declaration_fetch.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/domain/services/declaration_fetch.rs:64), and [declaration_ingestion.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/outbound/declaration_ingestion.rs:56).

The smallest diagnostic improvement is to retain status and request context before consuming the response, then include those plus a bounded response-body excerpt when status checking or deserialization fails. The existing error cannot reveal the actual upstream message after the fact. Both the member-list and declaration endpoints require `totalResults`, so the error alone does not identify which endpoint failed. See [parliament_api.rs](/Users/jamie/development/exposed/exposed/src/lib/outbound/parliament_api.rs:67).
